skill.description: Configure Groove task, memory, Git, and Groovebook settings, then write `.groove/index.md` and a matching `.groove/.gitignore`.

security_audit.summary: Most external-command alerts are Markdown inline code, not executable shell syntax. Hidden-file access is expected and scoped, but replacing `.groove/.gitignore` can erase user-managed entries.

remediation.suggestion: Preserve unmanaged entries or show a diff and require confirmation before replacing the file.

content.value_statement: Groove setup requires coordinated task, memory, Git, and sharing settings. This skill collects validated choices and writes consistent repository configuration files.
actual_capabilities: Reads existing `.groove/index.md` values and presents them as defaults.
Guides users through task storage, display limits, memory review, Git, and Groovebook settings.
Accepts default mode or key-value arguments for unattended configuration.
Writes `.groove/index.md` with confirmed settings and the installed Groove version.
Generates `.groove/.gitignore` entries from memory, task, and hook strategies.
Warns when the root `.gitignore` would override Groove commit settings.
limitations: Configures Groove settings only; it does not install task backends.
Replaces `.groove/.gitignore`, which can remove entries maintained outside this workflow.
Depends on an installed Groove skill file to determine the version.
Does not automatically resolve conflicts in the repository root `.gitignore`.

use_cases.title: Prepare a New Repository
use_cases.description: Create a complete Groove configuration with guided choices before installing task backends.
use_cases.target_user: Developer starting Groove in a repository

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Settings
use_cases.description: Choose shared Git, task, memory, and Groovebook policies for a collaborative repository.

use_cases.title: Update Existing Configuration
use_cases.description: Review current values, change selected settings, and regenerate matching ignore rules.

prompt_templates.title: Interactive Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure Groove interactively for this repository. Explain each setting before asking me to confirm it.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Defaults
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the Groove configuration using defaults. Show the final values and files changed.

prompt_templates.title: Set Selected Values
prompt_templates.prompt: Set tasks.storage to linear and git.memory to hybrid. Use defaults for unspecified settings, then summarize the result.

prompt_templates.title: Review Team Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the existing Groove configuration. Preserve suitable values, propose team collaboration changes, and apply only choices I confirm.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an established repository

output: Configured the Beans task backend with list limit 15 and analysis limit 30.
Set five memory review days and local-only memory and task files.
Prepared the repository for Groove backend installation.

output_examples.input: Use Linear, keep memory sessions local, and share hooks.
output_examples.output: The configuration uses Linear tasks, hybrid memory tracking, and shared hooks. Generated ignore rules keep memory sessions and cache files local.

output_examples.input: Review my current settings before updating them.
output_examples.output: Current values are presented for confirmation. Only approved changes are written, followed by a summary of configuration and Git strategy.

best_practices: Review Git strategies before writing files, especially when configuration data may contain private information.
Inspect the final summary and generated ignore rules before installing task backends.
Commit shared configuration changes separately so teammates can review repository behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not use unattended defaults when repository privacy requirements are unknown.
Do not keep manual entries only in `.groove/.gitignore`, because this skill replaces that file.
Do not assume commit-all works when the root `.gitignore` excludes the entire `.groove` directory.

faq.question: Does this skill install task backends?
faq.answer: No. It prepares configuration and then directs you to the separate Groove installation skill.

faq.question: What happens when configuration already exists?
faq.answer: The skill reads current values and presents each one for confirmation or replacement.

faq.question: Which task backends are supported?
faq.answer: It configures Beans, Linear, GitHub, or no task backend.

faq.question: How are Groove files tracked in Git?
faq.answer: Memory, task, and hook strategies determine which generated paths are ignored or committed.

faq.question: Can Groovebook sharing be disabled?
faq.answer: Yes. Leave the Groovebook repository value blank to disable sharing.

faq.question: Will it change the root `.gitignore`?
faq.answer: No. It warns about conflicting root rules but leaves their resolution to the user.
